title: Device Health Monitoring Automation with Claude
tagline: From VIP, HA and version checks to the right ServiceNow ticket, automatically
audience: Network operations, load balancer and data centre engineers, NOC leads, ITSM and automation teams running F5, NetScaler, Radware, other load balancers (Anaya LB) and Cisco ACI
prerequisites: Working knowledge of load balancers (VIPs, pools, HA pairs, config sync)
Basic REST API and JSON concepts
Familiarity with ServiceNow incidents and change requests is helpful, not required
outcomes: Define a platform-neutral health model covering VIP status, uptime, HA state, sync state, version and last change for every device class
Collect health signals from F5 iControl REST and tmsh, Citrix NetScaler NITRO, Radware Alteon via Cyber Controller, other load balancers (Anaya LB) and Cisco APIC REST
Use Claude with tool use and structured JSON outputs to turn raw evidence into a cited, severity-ranked health verdict
Create or update ServiceNow incidents through the Table API and Flow Designer with deduplication and correlation IDs
Run the whole workflow on a schedule under approvals, guardrails and a complete audit trail

modules.title: What device health means across the fleet
topics: The six health signals: VIP status, uptime, HA status, sync status when in HA, software version and last change performed
How each signal looks on F5 BIG-IP, Citrix NetScaler, Radware Alteon, other load balancers (Anaya LB) and Cisco ACI
Why manual morning checks fail: missed sync drift, stale tickets, duplicate incidents
The pattern for the whole course: Claude plans and explains, deterministic code executes, a person approves, everything is logged
modules.lab: Walk the lab fleet by hand with tmsh, NITRO and the APIC GUI and record what a healthy baseline looks like for each platform.

modules.title: Setting up Claude Code, the Agent SDK and MCP for this workflow
topics: Installing Claude Code, project CLAUDE.md conventions and the Agent SDK in Python
Building a read-only MCP server that exposes get_vip_status, get_ha_state and get_version tools over the lab devices
Tool use and structured JSON outputs: defining a HealthReading schema with Pydantic
Secrets handling for device and ServiceNow credentials outside the model context
modules.lab: Scaffold the project with Claude Code, run the MCP server locally and have the agent read the version of lb-f5-01 through a tool call.
modules.deliverable: Working agent project with a read-only device MCP server.

modules.title: Collecting health from F5 and NetScaler
topics: F5 iControl REST: /mgmt/tm/ltm/virtual/stats for VIP availability, /mgmt/tm/cm/device and /mgmt/tm/cm/sync-status for HA and sync, /mgmt/tm/sys/version
tmsh equivalents (show sys failover, show cm sync-status, show sys version) for devices without REST access
NetScaler NITRO: /nitro/v1/stat/lbvserver, /nitro/v1/config/hanode, /nitro/v1/config/nsversion and system uptime
Normalising every response into the shared HealthReading schema with retries and timeouts
modules.lab: Write the F5 and NetScaler collectors with Claude Code, inspect every diff, and run them against the lab HA pairs.
modules.deliverable: F5 and NetScaler collectors with pytest fixtures.

modules.title: Collecting health from Radware, other load balancers (Anaya LB) and Cisco ACI
topics: Radware Alteon health through Cyber Controller REST and SNMP: virtual server state, VRRP peer status, sync status, image version
A generic adapter interface for other load balancers (Anaya LB) and devices that only offer CLI or SNMP
Cisco APIC REST API: topSystem and fabricNode for uptime and role, firmwareRunning for version, fabricHealthTotal for fabric health
Handling partial data: marking a signal as unknown rather than guessing
modules.lab: Add the Alteon, generic and APIC collectors and prove a missing signal surfaces as unknown, not healthy.

modules.title: Last change performed: correlating config history and change records
topics: F5 audit log via tmsh show sys log audit (or /var/log/audit) and sync events in /var/log/ltm, NetScaler ns.log and config save timestamps, APIC audit log via the aaaModLR class
Pulling closed and scheduled change requests from the ServiceNow change_request table for each configuration item
Git-tracked configuration snapshots and diffs as a second source of truth
Building a timeline that links a health change to the last change performed on the device
modules.lab: Make a controlled change on lb-ns-02, then watch the pipeline find it in the device log, the Git snapshot and the ServiceNow change record.

modules.title: Claude as the triage analyst: structured health verdicts
topics: A HealthVerdict schema: severity, affected signals, cited evidence, likely cause, recommended action, confidence
Prompting with evidence bundles and forbidding conclusions without a cited reading
Severity rules as code: sync drift in an HA pair is never below major, a single VIP down on a standby is informational
Testing the analyst with contradictory and missing evidence
modules.lab: Build the triage agent with the Agent SDK, feed it twenty synthetic evidence bundles and score its verdicts against the rules.
modules.deliverable: Triage agent with verdict test suite.

modules.title: Creating or updating ServiceNow tickets
topics: ServiceNow Table API: incident create, query by correlation_id and cmdb_ci, update work notes and state
Decision logic: update the open ticket, reopen a resolved one, or create new, and never create duplicates
Flow Designer flows that assign, notify and set priority from the verdict severity
Idempotent runs and dry-run mode that prints the ticket payload without sending it
modules.lab: Run the pipeline twice against a failing HA pair and prove it creates one incident, then updates it with new work notes.
modules.deliverable: ServiceNow ticket adapter with dedup logic.

modules.title: Guardrails, approvals and audit for health monitoring
topics: Read-only by default: the MCP server exposes no write tools to devices
Approval gates for consequential actions: ticket priority P1 and P2, reopening resolved tickets, paging on-call
Audit record for every run: readings, prompt, verdict, ticket action, approver and timestamps in SQLite
Rate limits, timeouts and circuit breakers so a flapping device cannot flood ServiceNow
modules.lab: Add the approval gate and audit log, then trigger a P1 verdict and watch the run pause until a person approves.

modules.title: Scheduling and running the workflow with GitHub Actions
topics: Repository layout, pull requests for every collector or rule change and required reviews
GitHub Actions on a schedule and on demand, with secrets and a self-hosted runner that can reach the devices
Run summaries as job artifacts and a daily health digest posted back to ServiceNow
Handling device maintenance windows and planned downtime without false tickets
modules.lab: Ship the pipeline through a pull request, run it from Actions on a schedule and suppress alerts during a declared maintenance window.
modules.deliverable: Scheduled, reviewed and versioned monitoring pipeline.

modules.title: Testing, dashboards and operations
topics: pytest suites for collectors, severity rules and ticket decision logic with recorded API fixtures
Exporting health readings to Prometheus and a Grafana fleet dashboard beside the ticket flow
Operator runbook: what to do when a collector fails, when a verdict is wrong, when ServiceNow is down
Measuring the outcome: time to ticket, duplicate rate, false positives
modules.lab: Break a collector on purpose, watch the dashboard and the audit log explain it, and write the runbook entry.
modules.deliverable: Test suite, dashboard and operator runbook.

modules.title: Capstone: end-to-end device health monitoring for a mixed fleet
topics: Fleet in, verdicts out, with the right ServiceNow ticket created or updated and nothing consequential without approval
Scheduled GitHub Actions run against the full lab fleet with the approval gate and audit log exercised end to end
Dry-run and live run compared, with duplicate-ticket and false-positive checks against the acceptance criteria
Limitations statement, operator handover and team demo
modules.lab: Capstone build and demo on the full lab fleet.

capstone: A scheduled platform that collects VIP, uptime, HA, sync, version and last-change evidence from F5, NetScaler, Radware, other load balancers (Anaya LB) and Cisco ACI, lets Claude produce a cited health verdict, and creates or updates the correct ServiceNow ticket with approvals and a full audit trail.

narration: hook
Forty devices. One morning check. And someone still logs in to every box to ask if it is healthy.
hook

What if an agent checked every V I P, every H A pair, every sync state and every version, worked out what changed, and raised the right ServiceNow ticket before your first coffee? That is device health monitoring, done with Claude, done safely.
intro
Gennoor Tech presents Device Health Monitoring Automation with Claude.
story

Six signals in. One verdict out. You build the platform in eleven increments, and every increment is something you can test, review and demonstrate. Claude plans the code and explains the evidence. Deterministic Python does the collecting. A person approves anything that matters. And everything is logged.
path0

You start by defining what healthy actually means. V I P status, uptime, H A status, sync status when a pair is in H A, software version, and the last change performed on the device. You map each signal to F5, NetScaler, Radware, other load balancers, and Cisco A C I. Then you set up Claude Code, the Agent S D K and an M C P server that exposes read-only device tools, with credentials kept well outside the model.
path0

Then the collectors. F5 iControl REST and t m s h for virtual server stats, failover state and sync status. The NetScaler NITRO A P I for load balancing virtual servers, H A nodes and version. Radware Alteon through Cyber Controller, a generic adapter for other load balancers, and the Cisco A P I C REST A P I for fabric nodes, firmware and health. Every reading lands in one shared schema, and a missing signal is marked unknown, never assumed healthy.
path1

On day two you answer the question every N O C asks first. What changed? You pull audit logs from the devices, configuration snapshots from Git, and change requests from ServiceNow, and build a timeline for every device. Then Claude becomes the triage analyst. It receives the evidence bundle and returns a structured verdict: severity, affected signals, cited readings, likely cause and recommended action. No citation, no conclusion. And the severity rules live in code, so a sync failure in an H A pair is never quietly downgraded.
path2

Next, the ticket. Through the ServiceNow Table A P I the pipeline looks up the open incident by correlation I D, decides whether to update it, reopen it or create a new one, and never creates a duplicate. Flow Designer handles assignment and notification. Then the guardrails. The M C P server has no write tools for devices. Priority one and priority two tickets wait for a person. Every run writes its readings, prompt, verdict, ticket action and approver to an audit log, and a flapping device cannot flood your queue.
path3

Day three is operations. The pipeline ships through a GitHub pull request, runs from GitHub Actions on a schedule using a runner that can reach the devices, and respects declared maintenance windows so a planned upgrade never becomes a false incident.
path3

You add pytest suites for the collectors, the severity rules and the ticket logic, export readings to Prometheus, and put a Grafana fleet dashboard beside the ticket flow. Then you write the runbook for the days when a collector fails, a verdict is wrong, or ServiceNow itself is down. And you measure the outcome: time to ticket, duplicate rate and false positives, so the platform proves its own value.
labs

Every lab runs against a lab fleet of F5, NetScaler, Radware and A C I devices with synthetic faults. Nothing touches production. You will break sync on purpose, upgrade one side of a pair, pull a collector out from under the agent, and watch the pipeline explain exactly what happened.
stats
Eleven build steps. Three days, hands-on. Five device platforms covered. And zero duplicate tickets.
who
